newsitem.title: INDIA: Miss World pageant begins amid suicide threats.
newsitem.headline: Miss World pageant begins amid suicide threats.

text.p: The Miss World beauty contest opened on Saturday in a heavily guarded stadium in southern India, undeterred by threats by militant women to commit suicide by immolation.

The finale of the two-week pageant, with 88 contestants, opened to the sound of conch shells in Bangalore city, where earlier on Saturday police clashed with protesters and detained more than 1,000 people.

Dozens of local dancers dressed in shimmering blue skirts twirled before a large screen depicting images of ancient Hindu temples at the start of the event, which organisers said would be seen by more than two billion television viewers worldwide.
The pageant has been dogged for more than two months by protesters, who claim it demeans women and undermines India's 5,000-year-old cultural heritage.

Only hours before the start of the contest, three separate demonstrations led by right-wing Hindu nationalists left clouds of tear gas over roads leading to the stadium. Police said about 500 people had been detained.

Earlier, police said they had rounded up about 550 people to deter trouble. But the leader of a group of women who had threatened to set themselves on fire in the stadium after swallowing cyanide remained at large, police added.
